message.content:
Below are two ways to spin up a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Important**  
> * Google Cloud does **not** use the “EC2” terminology – that’s AWS.  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled, the **Compute Engine API** turned on, and the **GPU quota** (and any required GPU‑specific quotas) granted for the zone you choose.  
> * The RTX A6000 is available as the GPU type `nvidia-tesla-a6000`.  
> * The instance must be created in a zone that supports GPUs (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `europe-west4-a`, etc.).  

---

## 1. gcloud CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1️⃣  Set your project and zone
gcloud config set project YOUR_PROJECT_ID
gcloud config set compute/zone us-central1-a   # <-- pick a GPU‑capable zone

# 2️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --machine-type n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
  --image-family ubuntu-2004-lts \        # Ubuntu 20.04 LTS
  --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size 100GB \                # size of the boot disk
  --boot-disk-type pd-ssd \               # SSD boot disk
  --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --maintenance-policy TERMINATE \        # optional: how to handle preemptions
  --restart-on-failure \                 # optional: auto‑restart
  --metadata startup-script='#!/bin/bash
    # Install NVIDIA drivers (if not already installed by the image)
    sudo apt-get update
    sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
    # Verify GPU
    nvidia-smi
  '
```

### What the command does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size/type` | Size & type of the boot disk |
| `--accelerator` | Attach one RTX A6000 GPU |
| `--metadata startup-script` | Optional script that runs on first boot (here we install NVIDIA drivers and run `nvidia-smi`) |

> **Tip:** If you need more GPUs or a different machine type, adjust the `--machine-type` and `--accelerator` flags accordingly.

---

## 2. REST API (curl example)

If you prefer to use the raw Compute Engine REST API, here’s a minimal `curl` request that creates the same instance.

```bash
# 1️⃣  Obtain an OAuth 2.0 access token (replace with your own method)
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

# 2️⃣  Define variables
PROJECT="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# 3️⃣  Build the JSON payload
read -r -d '' INSTANCE_JSON <<EOF
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\\napt-get update\\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\\nnvidia-smi"
      }
    ]
  }
}
EOF

# 4️⃣  POST the request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$INSTANCE_JSON"
```

### Explanation of the JSON payload

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `name` | Instance name |
| `machineType` | Full URL to the machine type (`n1-standard-8`) |
| `disks[0]` | Boot disk configuration (Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image, 100 GB SSD) |
| `networkInterfaces[0]` | Default VPC network with external NAT |
| `accelerators[0]` | One RTX A6000 GPU |
| `metadata.items[0]` | Startup script that installs NVIDIA drivers and runs `nvidia-smi` |

> **Note:**  
> * The `acceleratorType` URL must match the zone you’re using.  
> * If you need to add more GPUs, increase `acceleratorCount`.  
> * The `startup-script` is optional but handy for installing drivers automatically.

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✔️ | Project ID & billing enabled |
| ✔️ | Compute Engine API enabled |
| ✔️ | GPU quota for `nvidia-tesla-a6000` in chosen zone |
| ✔️ | `gcloud` CLI installed (or OAuth token for REST) |
| ✔️ | Zone supports GPUs (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `europe-west4-a`) |
| ✔️ | Optional: install NVIDIA drivers via startup script |

Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu
```

And verify the GPU:

```bash
nvidia-smi
```

That’s it! You now have a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance with an RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.
